gen-flavors-merriweather: Stocky, cheerful, drawn with one pen tip. Merriweather, a text serif with a tall middle band and soft thick-thin shifts, would read as cozy and refined across a long passage next to such a bold heading.
gen-fraunces-gf-cascadia-code: Bookish up top, wiry below. If Fraunces were shrunk small, its open curves would lose some presence, while Cascadia Code, a monoline sans-serif with wide gaps between letters and tall lowercase, would sprawl if enlarged.
gen-fraunces-gf-cascadia-mono: Dignified Fraunces opens its curves and varies its line thickness moderately. But Cascadia Mono, a plain sans with curves as thick as its stems, stands letters like pins in a wide board, so a long passage ticks along steadily.
gen-fraunces-gf-julius-sans-one: Generous curve openings and understated thick-thin contrast mark Fraunces as the bookish one. But Julius Sans One has no modulation at all, with big gaps between letters, so a long passage would feel spacious and light.
gen-fraunces-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa reads wide and plain, with stubby ascenders and a big x-height, like cable bent into shapes. Fraunces handles the heading with a mild thick-thin variation, so the two feel dignified up top and open below.
gen-fraunces-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga lays down flat, single-weight strokes with generous tracking, like a router bit cutting each letter. And Fraunces above it keeps a measured thick-thin ratio, so a long read moves along unhurried.
gen-fraunces-gf-lexend-mega: Round, friendly, and tall in the lowercase. Fraunces earns its place in big, short headings, where its dignified, bookish curves have room, while Lexend Mega keeps its one-nib look underneath.
gen-fraunces-gf-lexend-tera: Fraunces brings a restrained thick-thin rhythm and a bookish, dignified air to big, short headings. But Lexend Tera sets its letters apart like stepping stones, with a plotter-pen line that never swells at a curve.
gen-fraunces-gf-lexend-zetta: Tall-bodied small letters, widely tracked, drawn like cut ribbon: that is how Lexend Zetta reads. Lexend Zetta holds one width throughout, while Fraunces thins only slightly at its hairlines, so the pair feels approachable and bookish together.
gen-fraunces-gf-montserrat-alternates: Chalk-board lowercase crowds toward the capital line here, with curves whose edges run parallel all the way round. Fraunces and Montserrat Alternates differ most in stroke: one has stress, the other none.
gen-freckle-face-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: BhuTuka Expanded One reads slowly, almost a leisurely walk. Freckle Face sits against its curvy, unclamped classic serif letters with fat crossbars and an organic, commanding presence.
gen-freckle-face-gf-hepta-slab: Freckle Face arrives with crossbars as fat as the stems they join, organic and commanding, against a stretched-out slab body. Hepta Slab is bookish and open, its counters breathing freely.
gen-freckle-face-gf-padyakke-expanded-on: Crossbars as fat as the stems they join give Freckle Face its organic, commanding look, and it makes a strong start. Padyakke Expanded One answers with wide-mouthed c shapes and spread-out glyphs.
gen-freckle-face-gf-stint-ultra-expanded: Stint Ultra Expanded has each character floating apart from the rest, with open counters leading outward. Stint Ultra Expanded would read like a traditional text serif with a pipe-cleaner feel, unhurried and authoritative beside Freckle Face.
gen-fredoka-gf-aleo: Fredoka draws friendly, rounded letters with a pen line that never changes width. And Aleo, a dignified serif, lets the eye slip in and out of its counters, so it handles the reading while the heading handles the welcome.
gen-fredoka-gf-almendra-sc: Almendra SC is an authoritative serif whose mouths stay open on every c, e and a. Fredoka, meanwhile, is at its best with a monoline stroke from start to finish, friendly where its partner is formal.
gen-fredoka-gf-antic-slab: Fredoka's pen line holds one width from start to finish, with an open e leaving a clear gap, giving it a friendly look. Antic Slab, a serif with round bowls and wide s curves, reads steadily and editorially.
gen-fredoka-gf-arvo: A technical-pen steadiness runs through Fredoka, every stroke drawn with the same friendly, approachable confidence and an open e. Arvo, a traditional serif, lets its curves refuse to close and reads with dignity.
gen-fredoka-gf-belgrano: Belgrano is a classic serif with open-mouthed curves that stay clear, while Fredoka's flat, contrast-free letterforms sit above it. Over a long stretch, Belgrano reads in a traditional, unhurried way.
gen-fredoka-gf-biorhyme: Fredoka keeps its curves turning corners without any pressure swell. BioRhyme, a classic serif with widely spaced capitals and curve ends that stop like lifted brush strokes, reads in a bookish, refined way across a longer passage.
gen-fredoka-gf-biorhyme-expanded: Friendly and approachable, Fredoka holds a pen line like drawn wire, with an open e showing a clear gap. But BioRhyme Expanded, a refined text serif, is the one built to spread open gaps between letters and carry the words.
gen-fredoka-gf-biz-udmincho: Friendly describes Fredoka, whose letters carry no thick and thin parts at all, just one pen line. And BIZ UDMincho, a bookish text serif with a shallow terminal curl and wide gap, gives the pair its traditional backbone.
gen-fredoka-gf-copse: One pen line carries every round and stem in Fredoka, with an open e and a clear gap, friendly at a glance. Copse, a literary serif, shows daylight through every curved opening, so a longer stretch reads easily.
gen-fredoka-gf-cutive: Soft and round, then refined. Fredoka holds one constant pen width, with an open e, while Cutive, a literary serif, spaces its running text widely. Their strongest quality is the friendly-to-refined step between them.
gen-fredoka-gf-david-libre: David Libre is a classic serif with hanging, open terminals and a dignified air. Above it, Fredoka draws its letters with one rounded, unvarying stroke, so the body can be set a notch larger without the heading losing its friendliness.
gen-fredoka-gf-enriqueta: Literary and dignified, Enriqueta curves its strokes and stops them short of closing. Fredoka is best at soft, friendly headlines with curves that never thin, while Enriqueta is best at carrying the quieter, bookish text beneath.
gen-fredoka-gf-fenix: Fredoka leads with a friendly, rounded w whose strokes never swing between thick and thin, giving the top a cheerful look. Fenix, a classic serif, handles the editorial body work.
gen-fredoka-gf-gentium-plus: Fredoka looks like a single-weight outline, bent and friendly. Gentium Plus follows with wide-mouthed c shapes and a refined, classic serif texture, so paragraphs would feel open and unhurried.
gen-fredoka-gf-gowun-batang: Gowun Batang is a refined, literary text serif whose terminals are cut back to leave a generous gap. And if Fredoka's wire-bent s curves were shrunk down, they would lose the presence that makes them charming.
gen-fredoka-gf-inika: Inika reads as a traditional, classic serif, with a visible gap in each s. Beneath Fredoka's friendly heading, a longer passage would feel settled and old-fashioned, easy to move through.
gen-fredoka-gf-kay-pho-du: Kay Pho Du reads like a traditional text serif with hollow-reed counters. Fredoka's rolling-ball-pen lines up top echo that single-width trail, so heading and body feel like the same hand.
gen-fredoka-gf-labrada: Labrada is a dignified, bookish classic serif with wide openings on small letters. Labrada's gravity gives the pair its strongest quality, because Fredoka's single-width pen line keeps the top friendly.
gen-fredoka-gf-laila: Laila brings an editorial, traditional serif voice, with generous space between curve ends and the stem. Laila's traditional poise is the pair's strongest quality, set against Fredoka's rounded-wire strokes.
gen-fredoka-gf-montaga: Soft, stitched, a little unfinished. Montaga is a bookish classic serif whose pen-lifted curves leave loops open, while Fredoka's friendly single-width line gives the heading a plainspoken sturdiness above it.
gen-fredoka-gf-new-tegomin: Friendly and rounded, Fredoka draws every line with a single pen width, while New Tegomin brings a dignified serif with a ring-wide c. They feel like a smile beside a handshake.
gen-fredoka-gf-podkova: Fredoka leads with a pen line that never changes width, and its e opens with a clear gap. Podkova follows in a bookish text serif, and its broad c gives the soft top a traditional footing.
gen-fredoka-gf-rhodium-libre: Rhodium Libre is an editorial text serif whose brush ends lift away before each curve closes. Fredoka, up top, feels like pipe cleaner bent into letters, so the page moves from friendly to traditional.
gen-fredoka-gf-rokkitt: Single thick thread is the feeling Fredoka gives, every letter traced with an open e and a clear gap. Rokkitt's serif body has a c as open as a bent paperclip.
gen-fredoka-gf-sanchez: Approachable up top, Fredoka keeps a constant stroke from the top of each letter to the baseline. And Sanchez, a bookish text serif with a c opened like calipers, earns the dignified side of the pairing.
gen-fredoka-gf-solway: Friendly and soft, Fredoka traces its letters with one pen width and an open e, while Solway answers in a bookish serif with a flat, stencil-like weight. Fredoka is best at greeting; Solway is best at speaking with authority.
gen-fredoka-gf-yuji-boku: One unvarying pen line defines Fredoka, which makes its heading letters feel traced from a single thick thread. Yuji Boku, a dignified text serif, holds each stroke like a drawn cable and opens its c like a pulled-apart bracelet.
gen-fs-kalam-bitter: Cozy and hand-drawn, Kalam bundles its lines tightly and feels inviting from the first word, while Bitter sets a slab-serif below it. Bitter's big lowercase eye and see-through s make a long read feel dependable.
gen-fs-kalam-inter: Inviting and handwritten, Kalam sets the tone first. Its heading is at its best being casual and tightly bundled, while Inter, a plain sans, is best at big, open counters and smooth, tube-like lines.
gen-fs-kalam-mulish: Tightly bundled lines with a hand-drawn feel make Kalam the most distinctive voice here. And Mulish, a plain sans with no thick-and-thin modulation and horseshoe-open apertures, would carry a longer passage in a modern, approachable way.
gen-fs-kalam-poppins: Cozy handwriting up top, tightly bundled lines and all. Kalam is the one with the pen-drawn warmth, while Poppins does its best work as a plain sans with tall, sturdy lowercase and loose curves.
gen-fs-kalam-roboto-slab: Kalam looks hand-drawn and inviting, its lines huddled close together like a note passed across a desk. Roboto Slab follows in slab-serif form, structured and precise, so a larger size for the heading would feel natural.
gen-fs-oswald-noto-serif: Oswald stands tall and tightly knit, a confident display voice with real muscle in it. And Noto Serif takes over with a prominent x-height and a subtle thick-thin rhythm, giving the page a literary turn.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-hind-vadodara: Hind Vadodara has a spacious, tall-bowled look, with the same stroke thickness in every direction and wide terminal gaps. And Chubbo's marker-tip curves bring a casual, inviting looseness that loosens the whole thing up.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-tabular: Technical in spirit, yet the heading is bold. Red Hat Display draws its marker-like line with daylight inside every curve, and if it were shrunk down, Tabular's monospace spacing would quickly steal the lead.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-noto-serif: Red Hat Display draws a contemporary, marker-like line with no thick-thin pulse and visible daylight in every curve. Noto Serif, a text serif with a prominent x-height, brings a pen-like stroke variation that is the pair's real strength.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-zilla-slab: Glass-tube lettering meets sturdy slabs here. Red Hat Display holds a hollow, constant line with open curves, and Zilla Slab pushes back with a lower, technical slab-serif build and broad openings on every bowl.
gen-gf-aboreto-fs-erode: Commanding capitals, spaced wide and loose. Erode follows as a text serif with a tall middle band and gentle weight shifts, and a body this size set large would crowd out Aboreto's thin hairlines.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-domine: Aboreto stretches its letters wide with open bowls and a high x-height that makes its lowercase look big. Domine keeps a text serif's tall lowercase and compact ascenders, reading with a slight pinch and a refined, dignified hush.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-epunda-slab: Dignified from the first glance, with Aboreto's wide-spaced letters and thick-and-hairline diagonals leading the way. Epunda Slab carries a longer passage with tall rounded lowercase and a visibly gaping c, so it reads classic and open.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-esteban: Esteban reads gently, its thin strokes barely lighter than the stems and its lowercase running big beside the capitals. Aboreto, all wide gaps and ladle-shaped bowls, sets a showier tone above that text serif.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-fauna-one: Dignified is the first word for Fauna One. Aboreto delivers hairline-against-heavy drama up top, while Fauna One keeps its shallow ascenders and tall middle band for steady, literary reading.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-glegoo: Glegoo opens its tall lowercase with big counters and curves that never quite close their mouths. Aboreto flashes sharp bright edges against fat darkness, and Glegoo simply gets on with the sentences.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-graduate: Graduate spaces its letters generously, with capitals and lowercase nearly the same height and no thick-thin shift anywhere. Over a longer passage it feels bookish and unhurried.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-halant: Halant has a faint thick-thin shift and outward-pointing terminals, with a towering x-height that gives its lines real authority. Over a long passage that reads traditional and sturdy.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-hanuman: Hanuman reads traditionally, with a high-waisted lowercase and wide-set terminals on the s. Aboreto's heavy verticals and thin horizontals give it a bolder entrance, and the text serif follows quietly.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-headland-one: Dignified describes Headland One, with its well-spaced letters and gentle stroke variation. Aboreto does fat round bowls and hairline joins best, whereas Headland One does low-key, steady lines.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-hedvig-letters-serif: Hedvig Letters Serif reads with open curves and a sturdy, tall body, its upstrokes and downstrokes barely different in weight. Hedvig Letters Serif holds the page quietly while Aboreto's bold-and-hairline strokes do the shouting.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-kadwa: Heavy ink-black strokes and gossamer hairlines share every Aboreto letter, which gives the heading its commanding look. Kadwa, a serif with open curves and a large x-height, settles in below.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-marcellus-sc: Aboreto sets fat vertical strokes joined by filament-thin connectors, and that gives the heading its expressive pull. And Marcellus SC, a text serif with a worn-charcoal softness, makes the whole thing feel literary.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-noticia-text: Wide-spaced and swaggering, Aboreto towers over its page with bold strokes and hairline counterstrokes. And Noticia Text, a classic serif with generous entry curves, brings a low-contrast dignity that grounds it.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana: Noto Serif Hentaigana keeps its small letters tall and its curves open, with a subtle thick and thin cadence. Aboreto, meanwhile, pinches heavy curves into hairline ends, and the text serif simply carries on the quieter work.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-ovo: Aboreto stretches its letters wide apart, with stark weight differences inside each stroke, while Ovo keeps a tall middle band and spacious curve terminals. The classic serif body is the steadier of the two.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-piazzolla: Ink-heavy verticals joined by thread-thin diagonals give Aboreto a dramatic, widely spaced look at the top. Piazzolla follows with a classic serif whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, and the opened e feels friendly beside it.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-pridi: Commanding, wide, and a little theatrical, Aboreto pairs fat strokes with hairlines. Pridi, a text serif with small letters standing proud and generous gaps at curve ends, would keep a longer passage moving along comfortably without much resistance.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-scope-one: Scope One is a text serif with counters that spill outward and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height. Scope One's sturdy, compact shapes are the strongest quality here, set against Aboreto's bold verticals and whisper-thin horizontals.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-slabo-13px: Slabo 13px reads bookish and open, with large counters in its tall a, e and s. Slabo 13px, a classic serif, gives Aboreto's black stems and pale threads something sturdy to lean on.
gen-gf-aboreto-gf-suwannaphum: Suwannaphum, a text serif with a wide-open c and a high, squared-off x-height, sits under Aboreto's fat verticals and threadlike joins. Giving it a little extra size would help.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-gf-cascadia-code: Soft curves, short ascenders and big bowls give Abyssinica SIL a gentle, dignified lead over the wire-thin Cascadia Code. The sans keeps its neighbors well apart, so the page feels spacious.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-gf-cascadia-mono: Mild thick-thin shifts and short ascenders over big bowls make Abyssinica SIL feel smooth and unhurried. Cascadia Mono, a sans-serif with pin-like letters in a wide board, keeps a long passage moving at a plain, pressure-free pace.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-gf-julius-sans-one: Abyssinica SIL tucks short ascenders above big bowls, its verticals heavier, like a gently tilted nib. Julius Sans One counters with sign-shop vinyl lines of a single width, spaced wide apart.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-gf-lexend-exa: Short ascenders over big bowls give Abyssinica SIL its look, with moderate thick-thin transitions. Lexend Exa draws wide-open curves with no calligraphic swelling and stubby ascenders, so swell above meets flat lines below.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-gf-lexend-giga: Refined and dignified, Abyssinica SIL keeps its contrast mild, never stark. Lexend Giga supplies the pull: flat, pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin, opened up by generous tracking.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-gf-lexend-mega: Dignified up top, Abyssinica SIL keeps its hairlines present but not razor thin. Lexend Mega squeezes one steady toothpaste-like stroke with a body height close to the capitals, so the eye moves from fine hairlines to uniform strokes.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-gf-lexend-peta: Spaghetti-like strokes and wide-mouthed curves make the body text glide along. Lexend Peta handles that glide, while Abyssinica SIL does its best work in stems and hairlines with a modest gap in weight.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-gf-lexend-tera: Abyssinica SIL gives short ascenders and big bowls a refined, dignified tone, with curves that gently swell and thin. Give Lexend Tera a modest size; its plotter-pen letters already stand far apart.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-gf-lexend-zetta: Tall-bodied small letters in constant-width ribbon strokes, widely tracked, give the body text a blueprint-lettering feel. Lexend Zetta holds a steady line against Abyssinica SIL's modest swing in weight, so the two feel drafted yet dignified.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-gf-montserrat-alte: Contemporary lettering runs below, while Abyssinica SIL swells moderately above. Montserrat Alternates holds the best card: round letters whose rims match the stems, drawn with one-tip simplicity.
gen-gf-agu-display-author: Agu Display bends strokes like thin plastic tubing into loops, bold and unvarying in thickness. And Author, dignified with a slight swell on the bowls, stays pleasant in modest helpings.
gen-gf-agu-display-gf-bhutuka-expanded-o: Agu Display loops thin, tubing-like strokes in a bold, distinctive voice. BhuTuka Expanded One slows the reading to a leisurely walk, with curvy letters that feel unclamped and thin joins as sturdy as the stems.
gen-gf-agu-display-gf-hepta-slab: Agu Display loops its strokes like bent tubing, bold and a little odd, while Hepta Slab below it stretches out wide and open. Over many lines that serif body feels dignified and bookish.
gen-gf-agu-display-gf-kiwi-maru: Kiwi Maru has terminals that stop far from the stem. Its round, uniform o shapes and generous letterspacing, set under Agu Display's looping tubular strokes, give the pair a traditional, editorial warmth.
gen-gf-aladin-gf-graduate: Heavy, tight and impossible to ignore, Aladin fills the line's middle with its big x-height and no stroke modulation at all. Graduate follows with generous white between letters and almost no gap between capital and lowercase height, which is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-amita-archivo: Amita writes in a relaxed, hand-drawn voice with rounded, welcoming letters. Archivo underneath has a commanding x-height and curves that open outward, and that firm, editorial footing is what makes the pair work.
gen-gf-amita-fs-asap: Asap keeps its body height close to the capitals. Amita, by contrast, cuts its hand-drawn, friendly glyphs as if from strips of equal width, while Asap's open arcs are what make a sans text readable.
gen-gf-amita-fs-bespoke-serif: Amita brings a relaxed, hand-drawn friendliness, its diagonals carrying as much heft as its stems. And Bespoke Serif, a classic serif with thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones, feels authoritative but wouldn't suit endless paragraphs.
gen-gf-amita-fs-epilogue: Loose, friendly and a bit wiry. Epilogue brings curvy, unclamped letters with a tall lowercase and stubby ascender tips, and under Amita's moderate hand-drawn heading it reads as a taller, crisper sans-serif partner.
gen-gf-amita-fs-erode: Soft hand lettering meets a tall, gently shaded serif, with Amita's strokes never swelling like brush work. Amita is best at friendly rounded warmth, while Erode does best with its shallow ascenders and flowing contrast.
gen-gf-amita-fs-fira-sans: Large and crisp, with s curves opening wide at both ends and no stroke contrast at all. Fira Sans does the steady reading work as a plain sans, while Amita handles the relaxed, hand-drawn greeting.
gen-gf-amita-fs-public-sans: Amita sets a relaxed, hand-drawn tone, its rounded bowls never swelling or thinning in outline. Public Sans then supplies a hefty lowercase with broad open counters, giving the page a trustworthy sans-serif footing.
gen-gf-amita-fs-supreme: Loose, hand-drawn warmth up top, with Amita's rounded letters staying open and inviting. Supreme sits below in a crisp, heavy-looking sans, tall in the lowercase.
gen-gf-amita-general-sans: Relaxed and friendly, Amita writes its heading with a hand-drawn softness, while General Sans fills the line with tall, smooth-bending sans letters. Reading on feels steady.
gen-gf-amita-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: Friendly and relaxed, Amita hums along in rounded, hand-drawn letters over the heading. BhuTuka Expanded One brings a literary text serif whose curvy shapes slow the reading to a leisurely walk.
gen-gf-amita-gf-hepta-slab: Hepta Slab stretches each word out, its open counters breathing into the white space of a bookish serif. And Amita's hand-drawn roundness is the quality that makes the pair feel so approachable.
gen-gf-amita-gf-kiwi-maru: Amita writes a relaxed, hand-drawn heading, its rounded letters staying open and friendly from the first word to the last. Kiwi Maru, meanwhile, offers editorial text serif with generous letterspace.
gen-gf-amita-gf-orbit: Soft handwriting meets crisp type. Amita is best at rounded, friendly warmth, whereas Orbit, a plain sans with each character floating apart, is best at rope-like consistency in every stem.
gen-gf-amita-gf-padyakke-expanded-one: Hand-drawn friendliness leads, with Amita's rounded letters staying open and inviting. And Padyakke Expanded One, a literary text serif with pitcher-mouthed c shapes, spreads its glyphs wide beneath.
gen-gf-amita-gf-science-gothic: Science Gothic reads one letter at a time, with stroke ends set far apart. Amita is best at hand-drawn, relaxed warmth in the heading, while this sans is best at approachable, uniform strokes.
gen-gf-amita-gf-stint-ultra-expanded: Amita opens with a relaxed, hand-drawn warmth across the heading. Stint Ultra Expanded, a text serif with characters floating apart and open counters leading outward, makes a longer passage feel slow and traditional.
gen-gf-amita-manrope: Soft handwriting, then a tidy line. Amita is best at hand-drawn, friendly roundness, while Manrope, a plain sans with bright open curves, is best at holding one width throughout.
gen-gf-amita-montserrat: Amita writes its headings with a loose, hand-drawn warmth and rounded, inviting letters. Montserrat follows on a plain sans frame with oversized counters, so a long paragraph glides along like wire.
gen-gf-amita-satoshi: Satoshi stands tall on its high x-height, with wide-open e shapes and every stroke cut to one width. Amita is the loose, friendly hand here, while Satoshi does the quietly approachable work of carrying the text.
gen-gf-amita-switzer: Amita brings a soft, hand-drawn friendliness to the top, with rounded letters that stay inviting. And Switzer, a sans-serif of tubular, wire-like forms and a tall waist line, gives the pair its sharpest quality: a loose hand set against Swiss precision.
gen-gf-amita-work-sans: Hand-drawn and rounded, with a soft hum. Amita is best at looking relaxed and friendly in a headline, while Work Sans, set with a high mean line and c tips that keep their distance, is best at sounding modern and contemporary in the text.
gen-gf-angkor-gf-graduate: Heavy, stencil-like and commanding, Angkor spaces its tight-mouthed rounded letters far apart with a hint of modulation in the strokes. Graduate answers it with a pen line that holds one width, and its open letters.
gen-gf-anybody-gf-epunda-slab: Loud and distinctive, with gently flared curve ends. Anybody is best at making lowercase crowd up toward the caps, while Epunda Slab is best at dignified, classic serif text with a visibly gaping c and tall rounded forms.
gen-gf-anybody-gf-fauna-one: Bold in attitude, Anybody packs its lowercase up toward the caps and lets its curve ends flare without touching. Fauna One is best at a literary, dignified reading, with a tall middle band, shallow ascenders and descenders, and a generous e.
gen-gf-anybody-gf-glegoo: Glegoo reads as refined and editorial, with big counters in a tall lowercase and curves that keep wide, unclosed mouths. But the strongest quality is the jolt against Anybody, whose bold display letters crowd the caps and flare gently at the curve ends.
gen-gf-anybody-gf-graduate: Flared curve ends that stay apart, with a lowercase crowded up against the caps, make Anybody instantly distinctive in a heading. Graduate is the foil: a dignified text serif drawn with a pen-like line of constant weight.
gen-gf-anybody-gf-kadwa: Anybody packs its lowercase up toward the caps and flares its curve ends gently, so every heading looks bold. But the pair's real strength is Kadwa, a classic serif with open-ended curves and a larger-than-usual x-height.
gen-gf-anybody-gf-noticia-text: Anybody swings in bold and distinctive, its curve ends gently flared and its lowercase packed tight up toward the caps. Make it small and that swagger fades quickly.
gen-gf-anybody-gf-piazzolla: Loud and a little cheeky: Anybody flares its curve ends and crowds its lowercase up near the capitals, while Piazzolla's serif text stays refined. Long paragraphs feel authoritative and steady.
gen-gf-anybody-gf-pridi: Pridi sets a classic, refined text serif beneath a loud heading. Its small letters stand almost capital-sized with generous gaps at the curve ends, so Anybody's flared bold look gets a long, patient page to sit above.
gen-gf-anybody-gf-scope-one: Traditional in spirit, Scope One spills its counters into open space and pairs stubby ascenders with a big x-height under Anybody's flared display letters. Anybody grabs attention; Scope One holds it.
gen-gf-anybody-gf-slabo-13px: Slabo 13px brings a bookish, dignified serif with large open counters in its tall a, e and s, set against Anybody's bold flared heading. Drop the heading a size if it crowds the text.
gen-gf-arbutus-gf-cascadia-code: Cascadia Code reads as wire-thin and spaced out, each bend left clear and unobstructed. Arbutus, with its mild stroke contrast and big counters, adds a dignified serif warmth above that plain sans.
gen-gf-arbutus-gf-julius-sans-one: Spacious and gentle, Arbutus lifts a dignified serif heading with mellow modulation over Julius Sans One. Arbutus is best at classic warmth, while the sans-serif below does rounded, open-ended curves with huge gaps between letters.
